name: Summoning
description: Calling the spirits, the elementals and the dead are what is commonly thought of when Summoners are mentioned, but in fact, nearly any creature can be called to a thaumaturge who knows the right words to use and the right actions to take. The hunter that whistles up prey to be slaughtered, the horse trainer who can call in the herds from the field — they are as much summoners as the black cultist making deals with the Yozis' servants. A thaumaturge may choose to further limit one or more of their summoning aspects — a shaman might only be able to summon up the ghosts of his ancestors, for example. This halves the cost of the aspect and should be noted on the character sheet, as with Summoning (War Gods).

aspects.name: Beasts
aspects.description: Summoning and controlling the beasts of the wood and the field and the sky and the sea. Calling: spend one temporary Willpower and roll Charisma + Occult at a difficulty of (the creature's control rating - 2, minimum 1); calling range is one mile per dot of permanent Essence. Controlling: Manipulation + Occult at a difficulty of (the creature's control rating - 1).

aspects.name: Mortals
aspects.description: The thaumaturge must know the target's actual name, not a title or position, and must have a bodily sample (hair, nail clippings). A resisted action: Manipulation + Occult against the target's Willpower + permanent Essence. Exalted roll Willpower + (permanent Essence x 2), gain two free successes, and are always aware of the attempt and of who made it. Subtract one success for each orientation separating summoner and target.

aspects.name: Demons
aspects.description: Summoning a demon of the First Circle requires a Charisma + Occult roll at difficulty 3 and normally a human sacrifice. This forces the demon to appear but places no geas of command upon it: mortals cannot force a demon to perform a task. Banishing one the thaumaturge summoned is Manipulation + Occult at difficulty 2. Second Circle demons cannot be coerced into appearing; no demon of the Third Circle has ever been summoned by a mortal.

aspects.name: Elementals
aspects.description: Charisma + Occult at a difficulty equal to the elemental's permanent Essence. Summoned elementals are not coerced to serve and must be bargained with, typically for a sacrifice equal to their permanent Essence. They are forsworn from attacking the summoner for a day and a night unless maltreated. They will not normally serve more than a week, and no task may last longer than a season.

aspects.name: Ghosts
aspects.description: The summoner must go to the grave or place of death, or know the ghost's full name, and make an offering of blood. About 15 minutes, culminating in a Charisma + Occult roll. Difficulty 2 in Creation, 1 in a shadowland or during Calibration, +1 per century dead. An animal sacrifice adds one die, a human sacrifice two, a relative's fresh blood one more. Summoning with no Occult is +3 difficulty; Occult 1 is +2; Occult 2 is +1.

aspects.name: Spirits
aspects.description: A thaumaturge does not summon spirits, he beckons them. Roll Charisma + Performance at a difficulty equal to the spirit's permanent Essence; if successful the spirit must fail a Virtue roll dictated by the summoner or appear. The thaumaturge has no power over the spirit once it arrives, and the spirit's reaction is shaded by the Virtue invoked.

name: Warding
roll: Manipulation + Occult (Perception + Occult to detect weaknesses in an existing ward, Intelligence + Occult to determine the specific warding ritual required)
description: Warding is the simplest of Arts, and in nearly every community there will be a handful of people who at least know its basics. Wards are barriers against intrusion or contamination, sealing an area off from the being or influence they are designed to defend against. Wards come in two types: generic (proof against an entire class of creature) and specific (particular to a given type). They nearly always have a physical component — a line of salt or ash, sigils, woven dreamcatchers, statuary. For each day or portion of a day spent preparing, add one success to the ward's durability, and one success to its strength for every two days. Successes are divided between the ward's two attributes, Strength and Durability. Materials to ward a decent-sized home cost Resources 2; Resources 3 wards a large mansion, 4 a small town, 5 a small city. Long-term wards require maintenance, and unmaintained wards lose one dot of Strength and Durability per year.

name: Exorcism
description: Rogue spirits and the dead are often found harassing mortals — sometimes with justification, often without — and it is the duty of the ghost hunter or exorcist to send them back to their rest. Exorcism is broken up into three basic tasks. Placation: an extended Charisma + Occult negotiation requiring successes equal to twice the spirit's Willpower + Essence, one hour per roll, difficulty (6 - the spirit's Compassion), with a total number of rolls equal to the exorcist's Endurance (or Stamina - 2). Expulsion: driving a spirit out of a possessed mortal, an extended Manipulation + Occult roll at a difficulty equal to the spirit's lowest Virtue, requiring successes equal to twice its highest Virtue, each roll representing 10 minutes and costing a Willpower. Banishment: spirits cannot be banished or forced from a location for more than a few scenes; see the banishment table for rolls, costs, successes and durations by entity class.

name: Astrology
description: Mortal thaumaturges have, over the millennia, researched, stolen and otherwise acquired a surprisingly complete set of astrological ephemera — tables, charts, star maps and stellar associations that detail the effects the stars and constellations have on a person or group's destiny. Predictions are made using Intelligence + Occult at a difficulty of (8 - any dots in the Destiny Merit; heroic mortals always count as having Destiny of at least 1). Access to Varangian or First Age astrological machinery makes the base difficulty 5 rather than 8. Successes are divided between duration and accuracy, from one month and 'extremely vague, at best' at one success up to ten years and genuinely accurate at six or more. Predictions tend to come true if the gods or Sidereals do not meddle, but they need not be exactly accurate — they are often misleading, inconclusive or missing important details.
